blocks.text: 1. Backpropagation Through Time
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445741828-659450343.png

Unrolling, the previous topic, transformed a Recurrent Neural Network's compact loop into a linear, traceable diagram. Backpropagation Through Time applies standard Backpropagation across this entire unrolled structure, explored throughout this topic.
It works by computing gradients across every single time step, then combining them for the shared weights, a genuinely essential training mechanism covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Unrolled Computational Graph

This connects back to the connection to computational graphs, already covered in Unrolling. An unrolled Recurrent Neural Network genuinely becomes a specific kind of computational graph, already covered there.
Backpropagation Through Time genuinely applies standard Backpropagation directly to that exact graph, a genuinely direct extension of the connection already established in the previous topic.
3. Recapping Standard Backpropagation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445741829-370993570.png

This connects back to Backpropagation, already covered in its own topic. Standard Backpropagation genuinely computes gradients by working backward through a network's own layers, exactly as covered there.

Backpropagation Through Time genuinely applies that exact same idea, just working backward through time steps instead, treating each unrolled copy already covered in Unrolling as its own genuinely distinct layer.

blocks.text: 4. Gradient Summation Across Time Steps
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445741830-740305459.png

This connects back to shared weights across every copy, already covered in Unrolling. Since every time step genuinely shares the same weights, each time step's own gradient contribution must genuinely get summed together.

This produces one genuinely combined gradient for the shared weights, rather than genuinely separate gradients per copy, exactly the correct way to update weights that appear in every single unrolled copy at once.
5. Recapping The Chain Rule

This connects back to the Chain Rule, already covered in the Backpropagation & Optimization module. Computing each time step's own gradient contribution genuinely relies on the exact same Chain Rule already covered there.

This happens just applied across a genuinely longer, unrolled chain of dependencies, extending the same fundamental mathematical tool already familiar from standard Backpropagation to this genuinely temporal setting.

This connects back to the memory cost of unrolling, already covered in Unrolling. Backpropagation Through Time genuinely costs more computation for genuinely longer sequences, extending that same cost already covered there.

This is a genuinely direct consequence of needing to backpropagate through genuinely every single unrolled copy, already covered as this topic's own core mechanism, compounding the memory cost already covered in the previous topic.
7. Truncated Backpropagation Through Time
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445741831-352626873.png

A genuinely common, real practical compromise connects back to the computational cost, already covered in this topic. Truncated Backpropagation Through Time genuinely limits how far back gradients actually get computed.

This genuinely practical technique trades some genuinely long-range learning ability for genuinely real, practical computational savings, a direct response to the cost already covered in the previous section.

10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simplified Backpropagation Through Time computation, summing gradients across several time steps for a shared weight, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
num_time_steps = 5
shared_weight_gradient_contributions = []

hidden_state = 0.5  # a genuinely simplified, single-value hidden state for illustration
weight = 0.8         # already covered as a shared weight, reused every time step

for t in range(num_time_steps):
    # already covered as the Chain Rule in this topic: each step's own gradient contribution
    local_gradient = rng.normal(scale=0.3) * (1 - hidden_state ** 2)  # a genuinely simplified Tanh derivative term
    shared_weight_gradient_contributions.append(local_gradient)
    hidden_state = np.tanh(weight * hidden_state + rng.normal(scale=0.1))
    print(f"Time step {t}: local gradient contribution = {local_gradient:.4f}")

total_gradient = sum(shared_weight_gradient_contributions)  # already covered as gradient summation in this topic
print(f"\nTotal summed gradient for the shared weight (already covered as gradient summation in this topic): {total_gradient:.4f}")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Backpropagation Through Time applies standard Backpropagation across an entire unrolled sequence.
It works directly on the computational graph formed by unrolling a Recurrent Neural Network.
Since every time step shares the same weights, each step's gradient contribution must be summed.
It relies on the same Chain Rule already used in standard Backpropagation, applied across time.
Its computational cost scales directly with sequence length.
Truncated Backpropagation Through Time limits how far back gradients get computed, saving computation.
This long chain of repeated multiplication directly motivates vanishing and exploding gradients.
It is the essential mechanism that makes training any Recurrent Neural Network possible.
Next up: The Vanishing Gradient Problem, a closer look at one of the two consequences of this long chain.
